title: Цирк на кухне  (A Circus in the Kitchen)

segments.t: Back at Claude Monet, Senya and Fedya escalate their feud by sabotaging each other's plates right on the pass, turning the kitchen into a circus. Meanwhile at the hospital, Chef Barinov grumbles as a strict head nurse bosses everyone around the ward.
Мне это новый рецепт от Феди.
Вы здесь на кухне устроили цирк.
Не обращайте внимания, она везде свои порядки наводит.
Right, let's take their exchange slowly and unpack the Russian.
'How are you feeling?' The meaning hinges on 'how' working together with 'health' in spoken Russian.
'I am just thinking.' Senya brings out the contrast between 'there you go' and 'I think' in a few short words.
'Tell me, are you an idiot?' Fedya anchors the line on 'for me', while 'fool' completes the thought. Chef Viktor answers right away.
'What do you think you are doing?' Chef Viktor addresses the listener with the informal singular 'you' alongside 'are doing'.
'I do not know, look what he did.' Senya brings out the contrast between 'not' and 'know' in a few short words.
'I had nothing to do with it.' In Russian, the idea of 'I' flows naturally into 'what' without extra filler words. Chef Viktor answers right away.
'It was this moron Senya.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'this' before landing on 'Senya'.
Мне это новый рецепт от Феди.
'This is a new recipe from Fedya.' The grammar packs 'for me' and 'Fedya' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
'I do not care at all.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'yes' and finishing on 'do not care'. Chef Viktor answers right away.
Вы здесь на кухне устроили цирк.
'You two have turned this kitchen into a circus.' In Russian, the idea of 'you' flows naturally into 'circus' without extra filler words.
Не обращайте внимания, она везде свои порядки наводит.
'Do not mind her, she bosses everyone around everywhere.' Senya anchors the line on 'not', while 'to direct' completes the thought.
'She thinks she is the head chef.' Notice how Russian expresses 'thinks' and 'chef' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Chef Viktor answers right away.
'So just get some rest.' Chef Viktor anchors the line on 'like this', while 'rest' completes the thought. Now let's listen to the entire scene again without interruption.
